title: KV delta-sparse quantization experiment: asymmetric FP8 + sparse delta encoding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Experiment plan and running log for a hybrid KV cache compression strategy focused on asymmetric FP8 quantization combined with sparse delta encoding and per-layer adaptive thresholds. Goal is to reduce GPU memory pressure during continuous batching while bounding generation quality regressions across RAG and long-context chat workloads.
objective: Reduce KV cache GPU footprint by 2-4x on average across production request distributions, maintain <= 1.5% end-to-end token-level quality degradation on SQuAD/RAG-style evals, and verify stable latency under continuous batching with fallback hysteresis.
approach: Implement asymmetric FP8 encoding for low-magnitude KV vectors with per-layer scale and zero-point estimation computed offline from calibration traces
Add sparse delta encoding: store a full baseline checkpoint per attention block epoch and only persist deltas for least-significant sub-blocks when L2 delta < threshold
Integrate runtime profiler hook to emit per-request prefix length, KV miss/hit ratio, and delta-encoded size to Console trace events
Add a lightweight runtime hysteresis policy: if decoder perplexity drift > threshold OR tail-latency > target, gradually expand decoding to use full-precision cache for affected cohorts
Run controlled A/B against baseline on continuous-batching worker with realistic arrival patterns (mix of short chat, long chat, RAG retrievals).
datasets_and_workloads: Calibration traces: 5000 anonymized production prefixes (mixed short/long), sampled over last 30 days
Eval sets: SQuAD-style QA synthetic + RAG dev set (2k queries), long-context chat logs (1k sessions)
Load shapes: steady 200 rps continuous-batching, spike test to 600 rps, and cold-start sequences to observe KV warmup
metrics: median and 95th percentile tail latency (ms) under continuous batching
end-to-end generation ROUGE/L/EM on QA and RAG sets
fallback frequency and cohort-level quality recovery time
GPU memory alloc failures and OOM events
experiment_results_summary: Early runs (FP8 + delta threshold 1e-3) achieved ~2.6x reduction in average KV footprint on a g5.48x machine with mixed short/long workload
Token-level perplexity regression asymmetric: +0.9% on short-chat, +1.8% on long-context RAG when using aggressive delta threshold; visual QA EM drop 0.7% absolute

Hysteresis policy prevented visible user-facing regressions during synthetic spike test: when tail-latency exceeded 1.2x SLO, system automatically expanded to full-precision for top-5 cohorts within 3s (median), but fallback frequency increased write-amplification by ~6%
INT4 path (proof-of-concept) gave ~4.1x memory reduction but produced unacceptable quality degradation (>5% EM loss) for RAG; kept as offline-only archival tier
Sparse delta encoding added modest CPU+memory overhead for reconstructing blocks (~0.7ms median per-request), acceptable under current latency SLOs but will need optimization for sub-10ms targets

2025-02-02: Hysteresis policy prototyped and tested under synthetic spikes; identified write-amplification hotspot (logs/replication) and mitigated via batched flush (PR #5236)
